messages:
deploy-bot: [AUTO] SBOM / vuln-scan result for release 'canary/v2.3.0' -> FAIL
CVE-2025-1423 (medium) found in transitive package 'fastproto@1.2.3' -> pulled by 'proto-serial@0.4.5'
Exploitability: reported low; parsing path used by ingestion endpoint.
Policy: 'vuln-medium-transitive' -> block unless exception, canary+mitigation, or patch before GA.
Scan excerpt:
```
WARN: transitive CVE CVE-2025-1423 fastproto@1.2.3 -> proto-serial@0.4.5
Action: block release unless mitigation or pin+patch
```

dave_release: Heads up — deploybot blocked the GA. Need quick decision: pin, rollback, or accept with mitigation. @bob_sec can you triage?

bob_sec: On it. Quick Qs: is the vulnerable code reachable from hosted API? Any POC? If reachable we escalate. If not, we can consider canary+monitoring or short hold for patch.

alice_eng: We ran targeted fuzzing last night across ingestion. No POC found. Vulnerability is in proto parsing of an optional field we rarely use. We can add a runtime filter at the edge to drop that field. Upgrading fastproto ->1.2.4 available but requires rebuild + regenerate some artifacts (~3-4h).

carol_pm: Customer impact? If we hold GA, do we miss any SLAs or customer commitments?

frank_sre: If we want to move, we can run a canary at 10% and put a WAF rule to strip that field. I can push the WAF rule to canary and add a parse-failure alert and dashboard. Also can autoscale if errors spike.

emily_legal: From compliance POV we need documented rationale for exception and a ticket linking to the SBOM update + follow-up patch. If risk is low and mitigated, legal is fine with canary+patch, but need the record.

bob_sec: Proposed path: allow 10% canary rollout with runtime filter (WAF) + enhanced monitoring. Simultaneously open a pinned-branch with fastproto@1.2.4 and target hotfix within 8 hours. Update SBOM after hotfix and close compliance ticket. If a POC appears or error-rate >0.5% above baseline, rollback.

dave_release: Sounds reasonable. Plan: 1) enable 10% canary now (frank), 2) enable WAF filter to drop optional field (frank), 3) alice to open PR upgrading fastproto and pin the dependency on release branch, target hotfix in next deploy window (<8h), 4) bob to sign-off once PR exists and SBOM updated, 5) carol to draft customer-facing release note. I'll log decision in compliance tracker INC-2025-314 and update release notes.

carol_pm: Will draft the customer note: "minor dependency update; no user data impacted; monitoring in place" and link to INC-2025-314.

alice_eng: Starting upgrade branch now. Will aim for PR in ~2 hours. If anything blocks I'll post here.

frank_sre: WAF rule deployed to canary clusters. Dashboards: parse-fail metric + error-rate alert live. Canary deploy triggered (10% traffic) — watching logs.

bob_sec: :thumbsup: I will review PR when it's up. No final sign-off until SBOM is refreshed but provisional approval for canary with mitigation.

dave_release: OK proceeding with canary 10% + mitigation. Rollback criteria: any confirmed POC OR error-rate >0.5% above baseline for 5m. Documenting now.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: canary rollout started -> 10% traffic, 5 instances. Link: <deploy-url-placeholder>

frank_sre: Monitoring looks clean so far (first 15m). No parse POCs.

emily_legal: Noted in compliance tracker INC-2025-314. Please add SBOM diff when PR merges.

alice_eng: PR opened: "chore: pin fastproto@1.2.4 (CVE-2025-1423)" -> link to PR placeholder. Updating SBOM in that PR.

bob_sec: Reviewing PR now. If SBOM updated and CI green, I'll mark security sign-off.

dave_release: Good. Closing thread for now — moving to incident ticket for traceability. If anything changes, ping @here and we revert. :lock:
